provenance: Executor actually searched/opened primary sources on 2026-10-11. Headless workers did not fetch these pages: read_url was auto-denied. Treat supplied summaries as bounded evidence, no fabricated direct reading or quantitative effects.

g1.title: A Proof for the Queuing Formula L=lambda W
g1.author: John D. C. Little
g1.evidence: Original theorem relates mean number in system, arrival rate and time in system under stated stationary/finite-mean assumptions. Scope definitions must be consistent. Does not imply that increasing workers increases throughput or that transient 50-worker counts satisfy stationarity.

g1.title: How Do Committees Invent?
g1.author: Melvin E. Conway
g1.evidence: Organizing and delegating design constrains available designs; communicating groups must agree interface specifications. Coordination is required to consolidate subsystem work. Qualitative design argument, not a quantitative agent speedup theorem.

g1.title: Challenges in Measuring, Understanding, and Achieving Social-Technical Congruence
g1.author: Anita Sarma, Jim Herbsleb, Andre van der Hoek
g1.evidence: CMU-ISR-08-106 discusses aligning organizational coordination capability with technical dependency demands. It emphasizes measurement/understanding challenges. No numeric 50-agent capacity claim or universal optimal monitor ratio.

g1.title: DORA's software delivery performance metrics
g1.author: DORA / Nathen Harvey
g1.year: current official guide; publication year unverified
g1.evidence: Current model has five metrics, split into throughput and instability. Change lead time is commit-to-production, not worker uptime. Measure individual services in context; disparate aggregation and gaming metrics are pitfalls. Do not turn 50 active workers into the single success criterion.

g1.title: Handling Overload
g1.author: Google Site Reliability Engineering
g1.evidence: Queries differ in resource cost; QPS alone can misrepresent capacity. Separate resource accounting, graceful rejection/degradation and client-side throttling are discussed. Analogy to agent workloads needs evidence; never evade provider caps by adding endpoints.

g1.title: About protected branches
g1.author: GitHub Docs
g1.year: current official documentation; publication year unverified
g1.evidence: Required reviews, status checks, code-owner reviews and stale approval handling can gate merges. Merge requirements are configurable and require live repo verification; a merged commit does not prove deployment or visual acceptance.

g2.title: Grafana dashboard best practices
g2.evidence: Choose a monitoring question, reduce cognitive load, use hierarchy and comparable units. Document panels and ownership; avoid redundant dashboards and excessive refresh. Design guidance, not evidence of current live executor counts.

g2.title: Dashboards — Carbon Design System v10
g2.evidence: Prioritize important data, limit metrics, keep consistent colors/measurement systems and expose exploration via search/filter/drilldown. Older official v10 guidance, not latest component API. No unsupported whitespace percentage claim.

g2.title: Data table — Carbon Design System
g2.evidence: Tables support sorting, search, filtering and expandable rows for progressive disclosure. Pagination separates large sets; clear row actions and skeleton loading states aid scanning. Implementation may use plain HTML without Carbon runtime dependency.
